scope: Additional public inputs for the M0-M4 NBCP Hamiltonians and the bulk XTRG baseline. Existing Nature 2024 figure workbooks remain listed in ../../source_manifest.json.

files.description: Author-supplied TeX source and figures for the 2026 fan-phase preprint; authoritative source used for equations, representative coupling table, lattice constants, and modelling limitations.
Oxford ORA public data archive for field-dependent neutron/x-ray study; contains ASCII figure data, calculations, error columns, and plotting code. It does not contain a CIF.
Machine-readable public full text of the 2022 PNAS quantum-universality paper; used for lattice constants, AA stacking, interlayer-path cancellation, and experimental phase-boundary context.

Author TeX and vector/raster figure source for Gao et al. (2022). Fig. 4a supplies the published YC6x9 XTRG C_m/T heatmap and Fig. 4b supplies an independent zero-field XTRG entropy validation curve. Fig. 4d is classical Monte Carlo and is kept separately labelled.
Extracted Fig. 4 PDF used for auditable image/colorbar and vector-path recovery. Hash is recorded separately because it is the direct derived-data parent.
Official public MATLAB QMagen repository. Contains XTRG, SETTN, MPO compression, and triangular-lattice TLXXZ code.
Official Python front end. Contains ED but lists 2D XTRG as a future feature; used to rule out a ready Python XTRG path.

source_quality_notes: The arXiv TeX source is a preprint, not a peer-reviewed version of record.
The 2026 paper states that its interlayer parameter set is representative and non-unique.
The ORA archive supplies figure-level data and calculations, not original instrument event files and not a CIF.
For the magnetic dipole lattice only the Co magnetic sublattice is required; the cited sources establish a one-site AA-stacked triangular magnetic lattice and give a and c.

The older PNAS paper uses P-3m1 in its structural description, whereas the 2026 diffraction paper identifies the lower-symmetry actual structure as P-3. M3/M4 uses the latter and treats the discrepancy explicitly.

Gao et al. (2022) states that numerical data and code are available from the authors upon request; no author-supplied numeric Fig. 4 table was found publicly. The reconstructed heatmap therefore carries explicit color-scale and finite-cylinder limitations.
